last_assistant_message:
**[Rigby]: Both workflows fixed. They needed different treatment, not a copy-paste of boot — here's why.**

**`shutdown-cleanup`** — mirrors boot's shape closely. Verified step-01 (`step-01-purge-artifacts.md`) against the identity-loading constraint: it purges temp files and runs the root-check, doesn't touch `agents/master.md`/`SYSTEM.md`/identity — no exception needed at all. Now spawns one blocking subagent for all 4 steps, same pattern as boot.

One thing this surfaced that wasn't in the original ask: shutdown-cleanup's *real* trigger (per `agents/master.md`'s routing table) is "exit" / "log off" / "end session" — the words "shutdown" and "cleanup" never actually appear in how it gets invoked. Without a fix, the turn-level eval would never have fired for it in practice, making the whole correction dead code. Added `WORKFLOW_TRIGGER_PHRASES`/`_ANCHORED` to `eval-turn-start.py` for this. Caught and fixed two false positives while testing ("did you exit the meeting early", "the client wants to exit their contract early" both wrongly matched on bare "exit" until I anchored the single-word triggers to the end of the message).

**`weekly-review`** — does not mirror boot, and I didn't force it to. Its own frontmatter already names a distinct owning agent per step (Quinn for rocks/priorities, Shep for delegations/people, Chief for inbox/calendar, Sterling for social, Master for wins-and-misses/eval-summary), and it's interactive throughout — every step asks the controller something and waits for a real answer, not just at a guardrail-escalation point like boot. Collapsing all 8 steps into one generic `agents/master.md` subagent would have made this *worse* than the original bug (that subagent narrating Quinn/Shep/Chief/Sterling instead of actually being them). Instead: each step now spawns its own already-designated agent, with Master relaying that step's question to the controller and resuming the same subagent via SendMessage per answer — generalizing boot's single escalation-resume mechanism into continuous per-step interaction. Up to 6 `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` pairs per run instead of boot's one; confirmed `eval-agent-start.py`/`eval-agent-stop.py`'s existing link-into-open-turn-record logic needs no changes to handle that, since it only keys off `session_id` + `monitoring.active`.

**Verified, not assumed:** `load_master_workflows()` already picks up all three workflows automatically (just scans for `agent: master` frontmatter). Unit-tested `detect_workflow()` against 21 cases across all three workflows — explicit paths, slash commands, run-verb-adjacent matches, shutdown-cleanup's new natural-language aliases, and negative controls. All pass. All hook files compile; `settings.json` is valid JSON.

**Not done — no live end-to-end run** of either workflow's new dispatch model (no controller session to drive the interactive steps through); this is static/logical review only, same caveat as boot's fix.

`evolutions/.pending-changes.json` updated: `work-20260826-193329-eval-hook-lifecycle` now documents this closing round, including the two files touched this pass. Nothing committed. Say the word when you want it committed and packaged.
